title: Ford’s New Heritage-Coded Performance Car Succeeds Its Most Triumphant Claim to Fame
summary: The Blue Oval has revealed its Le Mans competitor set to take up the mantle from the car that upset Italy's finest.
content: The Blue Oval has revealed its Le Mans competitor set to take up the mantle from the car that upset Italy’s finest. Ford If you buy from a link, we may earn a commission. Learn more Sixty years ago, Ford made history with an authoritative performance at the 24 Hours of Le Mans, racing to a dominant 1-2-3 finish at the event’s 34th running in 1966. Welcome to Power Moves : Diving deep into the product and brand moves that can change where a category is headed. Discover more here . The competing GT40 was a monumental accomplishment, and not just for the brand. Beyond proving the Blue Oval could beat Ferrari, the car showed that the United States could hang with Europe. Today, it remains the only all-American competitor to take home the top spot. Ford Now, the Blue Oval has finally revealed the vehicle that’s set to carry the torch following such a triumph: the GT41. Ford’s GT40 follow-up In keeping with its predecessor, Ford named the car for its height. On the GT41, this reflects the distance from the ground to the air intake. Despite the shared conventions, six decades of progress have obviously yielded a very different machine. Even wearing a temporary pre-season blue-on-blue design, the GT41 is as low-slung as it is slippery-looking. That promise extends under the hood, as Ford is keeping the spirit of the glory days alive with a return to American muscle. The GT41 and GT40 are both named for their height. Ford To give the GT41 its giddyup, the Blue Oval is running a naturally aspirated 5.4-liter engine based on the Coyote V8. It’s a fitting choice, as the block was actually named after Ford’s first (not to mention incredibly successful) four-valve V8-powered racecar . Of course, as with other vehicles in the LMDh class nowadays, it’s capped in output, paired to a standardized hybrid system and built atop one of four approved chassis designs. Even so, the history is important. The intention, along with the various parallels, is abundantly clear. Ford’s aero isn’t lacking. Ford Still more to prove Toward that end, Ford’s film promoting the GT41 shows the company still has plenty to prove, even if its Ferrari rivalry is in the past. The undertones are hard to ignore. Directed by Zack Snyder and narrated by Matt Damon, it speaks to the same drive (and pride) that landed Ford at Le Mans all those years ago. The GT40 remains one of Ford’s most legendary vehicles because of its performance. Can the GT41 take up the mantle? Ford Moreover, Damon’s narration builds on a recent, distinctive connection to his performance as Carroll Shelby in Ford v Ferrari . In the same spirit in which his role steered the team to its first victory, the actor now rallies support for Ford’s return. The echoes don’t stop there, either. For instance, the “Go Like Hell” mantra is a Shelbyism , depicted in the film on a sign as Ken Miles (Christian Bale) screams past. Considering the shooting of the promo even took place at the same location as the hangar used for the workshop in the film, Ford has clearly gotten back into character. Ferrari better watch out, because the company still has something to prove. Ford will reveal the finalized livery ahead of the season opener next year. Ford Mark your calendars Ford’s GT41 will make its competitive debut in the 2027 FIA World Endurance Championship with the season opener in Qatar in March. The Blue Oval will once again brave Le Mans in June. Ford Ford GT41 Learn More About the Author: Gray is an associate editor at Gear Patrol, covering cars, motorcycles and anything else with wheels.
